beagle.fact: A scent hound with one of the keenest noses of any breed — often used as detection dogs at airports.

boxer.fact: Known for 'boxing' with their front paws during play, which may be where the name comes from.

bulldog.fact: Their loose skin and pushed-in face make them sensitive to heat, so they prefer short walks.

dachshund.fact: Bred to hunt badgers — the name literally means 'badger dog' in German.

german shepherd.fact: One of the most popular working breeds for police, search-and-rescue and guide work.

golden retriever.fact: Bred to retrieve waterfowl with a 'soft mouth' that carries game without damaging it.

labrador retriever.fact: Has a water-resistant double coat and an 'otter tail' that works like a rudder when swimming.

poodle.fact: Originally a water retriever — the classic show clip was designed to keep joints warm while swimming.

rottweiler.fact: Descended from Roman drover dogs and once pulled butchers' carts in the town of Rottweil.

yorkshire terrier.fact: Bred in Yorkshire mills to catch rats; their silky coat is closer to human hair than fur.
